What is JEE Advanced?

It is an entrance exam for admission to bachelor's programs in science and engineering at the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). There are a total of 18,160 undergraduate engineering/science seats across all 23 IITs , with admission through JEE Advanced. A few universities outside India, like the University of Cambridge and the National University of Singapore, also consider JEE Advanced scores for admission to their courses .

JEE Advanced exam is organised by one of the seven zonal IITs under the guidance of the IIT Joint Admission Board (JAB). The exam tests the skills and knowledge of aspirants in Physics, Chemistry and Maths. The JEE Advanced total marks, number of questions, and marking scheme are not fixed and depend on the organising institute.

Only those who qualify JEE Mains and are positioned in the top 2.5 lakh candidates in the order of merit can appear for JEE Advanced. Every year, around 1.8 lakh candidates take the exam, and 18% qualify on average, making it one of the toughest exams in the world .

Indian nationals interested in applying for IIT JEE Advanced have to score marks above the JEE Main 2026 Cutoff percentile . In addition to qualifying NTA JEE cutoff, candidates also need to fulfill JEE Advanced eligibility criteria 2026 of age, number of attempts, and year of passing the class 12 board exams in order to be eligible for appearing in JEE Advanced paper . Foreign nationals are exempted from appearing in NTA JEE Mains, they can apply directly for JEE Adv .

blocks.value: JEE Advanced Organising IITs

The exam is conducted annually by one of the 7 zonal IITs in a round robin rotation pattern. The exam is guided by the Joint Admission Board (JAB). This rotation system is essentially a way to ensure fair distribution of exam conducting responsibility among the seven zonal IITs.

You can prepare for all entrance tests at same time. It is a tough task but not impossible. For this a proper strategy is required. Here are some important tips.

value: Compare the syllabus: All engineering entrance exams have almost the same syllabus. There might be some additional topics in some exams. The aspirant must study the syllabus for all exams and find out the topics that are extra, and prepare those separately. Almost 90% of the topics will be common for all entrance exams, and hence, syllabus completion for one exam will lead to completion of the syllabus for all the exams.

Prepare for JEE Mains and incorporate the preparation for all other exams: Apart from JEE Advanced, all the exams are pretty straightforward for a well-prepared candidate. JEE Advanced require a higher level of preparation as the questions are multi-conceptual. However, the state-level entrance exams, and exams like BITSAT, VITEEE, etc., have direct questions. Most of the questions in JEE Mains are also direct and require the application of basic concepts. Hence, the candidates must prepare for one exam, like JEE Mains, that will cover their preparation for all other exams.
JEE Advanced needs extra effort: For JEE Advanced candidates must focus on time management and building exam day temperament. Learn how to apply multiple concepts to a question.

blocks.value: The bottom line is to prepare for JEE Mains to cover the preparation for all other CETs and exams like BITSAT and VITEEE. For JEE Advanced, work on sharpening your skills of time management, stress handling, multiple concept application, speed and accuracy.

Cracking JEE Mains and JEE Advanced is not possible in few days or months, it requires continuous efforts through two long years. If a student is focused and doing the studies regularly, revising the concept on daily basis and solving questions on each topic will definitely going to get success in first attempt.

faqs.question: How to prepare for JEE Mains 2nd attempt as well as JEE Advanced simultaneously also BITSAT and CET at the same time?
faqs.answer: You can prepare for all entrance tests at same time. It is a tough task but not impossible. For this a proper strategy is required. Here are some important tips. Compare the syllabus: All engineering entrance exams have almost the same syllabus. There might be some additional topics in some exams. The aspirant must study the syllabus for all exams and find out the topics that are extra, and prepare those separately. Almost 90% of the topics will be common for all entrance exams, and hence, syllabus completion for one exam will lead to completion of the syllabus for all the exams. Prepare for JEE Mains and incorporate the preparation for all other exams: Apart from JEE Advanced, all the exams are pretty straightforward for a well-prepared candidate. JEE Advanced require a higher level of preparation as the questions are multi-conceptual. However, the state-level entrance exams, and exams like BITSAT, VITEEE, etc., have direct questions. Most of the questions in JEE Mains are also direct and require the application of basic concepts. Hence, the candidates must prepare for one exam, like JEE Mains, that will cover their preparation for all other exams. JEE Advanced needs extra effort: For JEE Advanced candidates must focus on time management and building exam day temperament. Learn how to apply multiple concepts to a question. The bottom line is to prepare for JEE Mains to cover the preparation for all other CETs and exams like BITSAT and VITEEE. For JEE Advanced, work on sharpening your skills of time management, stress handling, multiple concept application, speed and accuracy.

JEE Advanced 2026 Analysis: Expectations and Predictions Based on Trends

JEE Advanced 2026 exam analysis will let the candidates know what the trends have been in JEE Advanced difficulty level, weightage, expected cutoff, exam pattern, marking scheme and thus give an idea about how to deal with exam preparation. On this page, we will discuss a detailed JEE Advanced 2026 exam analysis based on past trends. Also, we will look into some predictions about the JEE Advanced 2026 exam based on expert analysis.
JEE Advanced 2026 Difficulty Level

JEE Advanced has always been known for its unpredictability, difficulty level, and focus on conceptual understanding. While no one can exactly predict the paper, analysing past year trends gives aspirants valuable insights into what they can expect in JEE Advanced 2026.

Over the years, the JEE Advanced difficulty level has stayed between moderate to difficult. Usually, the toughness level alternates between moderate-to-tough and very tough, depending on the year. Note that, the conducting IIT do not play a role in exam difficulty level, thus the difficulty level of JEE Advanced 2026 cannot be predicted based on the IIT conducting it.

JEE Advanced 2026 Analysis: Key Takeaways for Aspirants

value: Focus on Concepts, Not Rote Learning: JEE Advanced rewards deep understanding. Questions are often based on mixed concepts, unlike in JEE Mains, where a question is based on one single concept only.

Prepare for Surprises: At least one subject will have unexpected twists, as seen every year. The twist can be in the form of exam format, questions being extraordinarily difficult or maybe the introduction of a new type of questions.
Improve Speed + Accuracy: Numerical-type questions demand precision. Hence, not only speed, but JEE Advanced also demands accuracy.

Do Not Neglect Any Subject: Even if Chemistry seems easy in one year, it can get tricky the next. Therefore, no one topic is more important than the other. treat all the topics available in the JEE Advanced syllabus with equal weightage while preparing for the exam.

JEE Advanced 2026 Preparation Tips
Given here are some important tips that will help you in preparing for JEE Adv exam.
Understand Syllabus & Exam Pattern

It is very important to understand the JEE Adv syllabus and exam pattern before you begin your preparation. The syllabus consists of topics from class 11 and 12 however, the difficulty level of the exam is way ahead of class 11 and 12. For this, students must build understanding of  the basic concepts using the right study material. The syllabus of JEE Advanced is vast and can only be completed if you start your preparation as early as possible. It is very important to complete syllabus as all topics in JEE Advanced are important. This is because, there are questions in the exam that carry concepts application from various chapters of JEE Advanced syllabus. Therefore, to solve one question, candidates must have a knowledge of various topics. Hence it is important to complete the entire syllabus of JEE Advanced with time for revision before the exam.

Also, the exam pattern of IIT JEE Advanced is very uncertain. There will be MCQs, matching type and NAV questions but the number of questions and marking scheme is not fixed. Candidates must be prepared for this uncertainty.
Make a Weekly Plan

Don't plan for a day because it might not be completed due to an unavoidable event on that day (you might be sick). If you plan for a week, you have other days to make up for it. Make a reasonable plan for JEE Advanced 2026 that you can complete by end of the week. If plan is feasible, you must not postpone it to the following week.
Also Check: JEE Advanced 2026: Hidden Lessons from Movies & Web Series to Boost Your IIT JEE Preparation
Refer NCERT Books for concepts

Your preparation should begin with the NCERT books. Read these books carefully and complete all back exercises. Try 'example problems' as well for more practice with objective questions. Keep in mind that reading and comprehending NCERT books are not same thing.
Also Check: JEE Advanced Marking Scheme 2026: Total Marks, Negative Marks, Section Wise Question Distribution
Create a Revision Strategy

You need to keep revising what you have studied. Concepts and basics of JEE Advanced must be on the tip of your tongue so that you are able to solve the questions in the exam with speed and accuracy. Also, form a strategy to revise. Do not invest equal amount of time in revising all the topics. Revise topics that you think you need more attention to regularly. Make notes while revising to retain the concepts in your memory. Check your performance after each mock exam and analyse what mistakes and patterns you are repeating and work on them.
Do Your Best to Prepare for Board Exams

All will go in vain if you don't score the minimum perentage required in class 12 for IIT admissions. You must give your all to the Board along with JEE advanced preparation. Unlike JEE Mains, the Board Exam contains subjective questions, so get in habit of answering them.
Which is more important: How long you studied or how much you studied?

If you feel you need to invest more time on a topic than increase your study time. However, if you waste your time in procrastination, then how long you study will not matter. Everything comes down to effective study. Utilise the time you study to prepare diligently without any distractions and with complete concentration.

Learn from Your Test Mistakes

Many tests are available, both offline and online. It is critical to develop habit of taking tests in the same format regularly. What is more important is that you learn from your mistakes in JEE Main and JEE Advanced Mock Tests. If you can correct those errors after each test, your performance will gradually improve all the way through. This is only way to bridge the gap between preparation and performance while also improving exam temperament.
Do Not Store Unnecessary Books

Start with the NCERTs to get hold of concepts and basics, and collect books that are good in the following categories: have a simple language and cover JEE Advanced syllabus have ample amount of question banks books that are topper recommended and experts trust books that work for you even if not recommended by experts and toppers
